objective: Prove the frozen minimal-counterexample target using SCC condensation and complete degree-0/1/2 extension cases.

atomic_claims.text: Every proper induced subdigraph of a vertex-minimum counterexample remains in the frozen class and has a valid acyclic 2-coloring.
The SCC condensation is acyclic; SCC-wise acyclic 2-colorings combine without a monochromatic directed cycle. Hence a vertex-minimum counterexample is strongly connected.
A color is blocked at a restored vertex exactly when there is a same-colored path from an out-neighbor to an in-neighbor in G-v.
Every valid acyclic 2-coloring of G-v extends when the underlying degree of v is at most 2, covering all incident orientations and both neighbor-color patterns.
A vertex-minimum counterexample to the frozen conjecture is strongly connected and has underlying minimum degree at least 3.

assumptions: Finite simple planar underlying graph; each edge is oriented exactly once.
Acyclic 2-colorings are maps to {1,2}; an unused color is permitted.
Minimality is by vertex count over all counterexamples in the frozen class.
risks: Natural-language proof draft only; no formal compilation or verifier receipt.
The lemma is a necessary condition for a counterexample, not a proof of the root conjecture.
Vertex minimality does not automatically imply arc minimality.
Declared Harness and importer digests await real remote gate validation.
